bug_description.normalized: The saved ASan report reproduces a 4-byte stack-buffer-overflow in `ihevcd_ref_list()` while decoding the staged 71-byte Annex-B HEVC witness. In vulnerable commit `072f9084f42730094e6d3cecf6078b3830577da6`, an earlier non-IDR slice on the frame-mode replay writes short-term-reference state into a reusable `slice_header_t` at `ihevcd_parse_slice_header.c:417-451`. A later IDR slice reuses that same slot without the missing `memset(ps_slice_hdr, 0, sizeof(*ps_slice_hdr));`; because `idr_pic_flag` is true, the whole non-IDR short-term-reference parsing block is skipped and the previously written selector / local STRPS members remain live. The final non-first dependent `TRAIL_N` slice (`00 20 6f`) then preserves that stale header state and skips fresh non-dependent parsing, so `ihevcd_ref_list()` reloads `num_neg_pics`, `num_pos_pics`, `pi1_used`, and `pi2_delta_poc` from stale short-term-reference data with no `MAX_DPB_SIZE` revalidation. The saved ASan frame report shows that consumed stale tuple drives `u4_num_st_foll` to the fixed 16-entry bound and line 179 writes the 17th `WORD32` into `ai4_poc_st_foll`. The fix inserts the missing `memset` immediately after slot selection so stale prior-header contents cannot survive the later IDR/dependent-slice sequence.

source.description: First project-code site where an earlier non-IDR slice on the crashing decode path materializes the short-term-reference state family later consumed from stale `slice_header_t` storage.
source.value_from: The staged witness is exactly `gt_results/arvo_17029/poc`, whose Annex-B NAL order is `PPS (45 20) -> BLA_W_LP (20 20) -> SPS (c3 20) -> TRAIL_N (01 20) -> IDR_N_LP (a9 20) -> TRAIL_N (00 20)`. The harness first calls `decodeHeader()` and then, at `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` lines 327-339, switches to frame mode and replays the original full `data,size` pair rather than the advanced local pointer from `decodeHeader()`. That replay re-exposes the earlier non-IDR slice bytes to `ihevcd_parse_slice_header()` once header state is loaded. Stage 01 artifacts do not isolate which earlier non-IDR slice arm later supplied the overflowing tuple, so the GT anchors `source` at the exact short-term-reference materialization site instead of a narrower raw-byte claim.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable decoder reuses a previously populated `slice_header_t` slot here without clearing it first, so later slice-header paths can preserve stale short-term-reference members across slice decodes.
root_cause.note: The fix commit inserts `memset(ps_slice_hdr, 0, sizeof(*ps_slice_hdr));` immediately after this statement. Without that clear, the later IDR and dependent-slice paths can carry forward older `i1_short_term_ref_pic_set_sps_flag`, `i1_short_term_ref_pic_set_idx`, and `s_stref_picset` contents instead of freshly parsed current-slice state.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The stale short-term-reference tuple has already advanced `u4_num_st_foll` to the fixed stack-array bound, so this store writes a 17th `WORD32` into the 16-element `ai4_poc_st_foll` buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` with `WRITE of size 4` at `decoder/ihevcd_ref_list.c:179`, and the frame layout shows `ai4_poc_st_foll` at `[128,192)` with the bad write at offset 192, one element past the array.

harness_replay.description: `decodeHeader()` advances only its local `data,size`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` then switches to frame mode and replays the original witness from byte 0, so earlier slice NALs remain available to seed stale `slice_header_t` state on the crashing path.

parser_admitted.description: After the header replay has loaded SPS state and the frame-mode replay reparses PPS from the front of the witness, slice NALs pass this gate and enter `ihevcd_parse_slice_header()` on the same codec instance that still owns the reusable `ps_slice_hdr_base` array.

fine_trace.note: Source. An earlier non-IDR slice on the crashing frame-mode replay reaches the short-term-reference parsing region and writes the short-term-reference family into the reusable `slice_header_t`: the selector bit plus either the SPS index or the local `s_stref_picset` body. Stage 01 artifacts do not isolate which arm later supplied the overflowing tuple, so the trace anchors the first exact materialization site instead of overclaiming a narrower raw-NAL arm.

Root cause. A later slice decode reselects a reusable `slice_header_t` slot here but, in the vulnerable revision, does not clear it first. The short-term-reference state written at step 1 can therefore remain resident until some later path explicitly overwrites it.

The witness later supplies an `IDR_N_LP` slice (`a9 20`). For that slice `idr_pic_flag` is true, so the entire non-IDR block guarded by this predicate is skipped after the uncleared slot has been selected. The IDR header therefore preserves whatever short-term-reference selector and local STRPS members were already in that slot instead of refreshing them from current-slice bits.

The final payload byte `0x6f` statically decodes under the admitted PPS/SPS state as a non-first dependent `TRAIL_N` slice (`dependent_slice_flag = 1`, `slice_address = 7`). This is the header-preservation path: it marks the crashing slice as dependent and, when a previous slice header is available, copies the prior header before any fresh non-dependent fields could be parsed.

depends_on.via: stale short-term-reference family in the prior/current slot

fine_trace.note: For the crashing slice this predicate is false, so the parser skips the entire non-dependent block that would otherwise repopulate `pic_order_cnt_lsb`, `short_term_ref_pic_set_sps_flag`, `i1_short_term_ref_pic_set_idx`, and `s_stref_picset` for the current slice. The stale short-term-reference family from steps 1-4 therefore remains live when the sink path is entered.

`ihevcd_ref_list()` converts the preserved header state into the loop tuple that drives the crash: it loads `num_neg_pics`, `num_pos_pics`, `pi1_used`, and `pi2_delta_poc` from whichever stale short-term-reference arm the header still selects. The parse-time clips in earlier non-IDR construction are not re-executed here, and this use site performs no guard that the selected stale tuple still fits `MAX_DPB_SIZE` before using it as loop bounds. With `runtime_disambiguation` disabled, the staged artifacts do not isolate which arm supplied the overflowing tuple, so the trace names the exact consumption site rather than asserting one producer arm.

fine_trace.note: The negative-picture loop begins filling the fixed `ai4_poc_st_foll[MAX_DPB_SIZE]` stack buffer from the stale tuple and advances `u4_num_st_foll` before the positive-picture loop starts.

fine_trace.note: The positive-picture loop continues with the same stale counts and the carried `u4_num_st_foll` cursor from step 7. By the crashing iteration, that cursor has already reached the 16-entry bound of `ai4_poc_st_foll`.

Sink. The first overflowing positive-picture iteration stores a 17th `WORD32` into the 16-element `ai4_poc_st_foll` stack array. This is the exact saved `WRITE of size 4` that ASan reports at offset 192 in `ihevcd_ref_list`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_17029-workspace /bin/arvo run` with the staged witness and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` / `WRITE of size 4` in `ihevcd_ref_list`, matching the public crash state `ihevcd_ref_list -> ihevcd_parse_slice_header -> ihevcd_nal_unit`.

format.name: Exact 71-byte Annex-B HEVC witness replayed in header mode and then again in frame mode
format.contract: Exactly the 71-byte file stored at `gt_results/arvo_17029/poc`. Its raw Annex-B NAL order is `PPS (45 20)`, `BLA_W_LP (20 20)`, `SPS (c3 20)`, `TRAIL_N (01 20)`, `IDR_N_LP (a9 20)`, and a final `TRAIL_N (00 20)` whose payload byte is `0x6f`. `decodeHeader()` advances only a local pointer, and `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` then replays the original full witness in frame mode, so earlier slice NALs remain available to seed stale `slice_header_t` state before the final dependent slice is parsed. The only byte-exact crash-site claim kept here is that final `0x6f` slice, which the vulnerable parser interprets as non-first and dependent; the staged artifacts do not isolate which earlier non-IDR parse arm last produced the exact overflowing short-term-reference tuple, so the contract is not generalized beyond this exact file.

evidence_limitations: The live `/src/libhevc` tree inside the staged workspace container is at later revision `d28f2210ee8e65afdfb07a1fd6582285d3d178e0`, not the sample's vulnerable commit `072f9084f42730094e6d3cecf6078b3830577da6`. All source-level locations and code snippets above were therefore recovered directly from `git show 072f9084f42730094e6d3cecf6078b3830577da6:<path>`, while the ASan caller-frame line 984 comes from the newer staged tree.

Because `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, the staged artifacts stop short of identifying which earlier non-IDR short-term-reference arm finally supplied the overflowing `num_neg_pics` / `num_pos_pics` tuple consumed at `ihevcd_ref_list.c:137-151`. The GT therefore anchors the exact parse, preserve, and use sites and leaves that last producer-arm choice explicit as a residual ambiguity instead of asserting either the SPS-backed arm or the local `s_stref_picset` arm without runtime proof.
